units.text: A deeper queue hides brief stalls because producers can continue while the consumer pauses. At 200 records per second, a 3-second pause requires room for 600 records. This is a sizing example, not a measured throughput gain. If the consumer is permanently slower, a larger queue only delays overload.

obligations.meaning: Capacity absorbs temporary consumer pauses by allowing producers to continue; it does not fix a sustained rate mismatch.
Retain the worked example and distinguish capacity arithmetic from a performance measurement.

units.text: First stop writes and record the current checksum. Copy the data to staging in batches of 128 records; do not replace the live directory yet.
Next verify the staging checksum against the recorded value. Only after it matches, atomically swap staging into place, then resume writes. On mismatch leave the live directory unchanged.

units.text: Dr Lin: In our non-randomized trial of 24 machines, the median fell from 80 to 68 degrees Celsius after the fan and firmware both changed. That is 12 degrees, not 12 percent. We cannot attribute it to the fan alone.
Operator Reyes: I disagree that this establishes a general improvement. Two machines overheated in high humidity; dry-room tests missed that condition.

units.text: The client timed out after sending the write. We do not yet know whether the server committed it. Retrying is safe only under the condition I will explain next.
That condition is reusing the same idempotency key: the server durably records it with the result. A new key could apply the write twice. Do not label the timed-out write a failure with no effects.

obligations.meaning: Timeout leaves commit status unknown, not an authoritative effect-free failure.
phrases: not a failure with no effects
